scope: Native EFI trace storage construction and scoped USB/independent-write controls; automatic capture remains unimplemented.

worker.environment: Disposable ARM64 KVM worker, retained 1.5.0 live root and private build volume

native_builder.command: sh scripts/make-efi-iso.sh world.tar DAEMONARCHY150AARCH64 output.iso new-work BOOTAA64.EFI

usb_control.transport: QEMU xHCI USB mass storage, raw writable image, EFI/KVM, four CPUs, 8 GiB RAM
usb_control.first_boot: No virtual RNG: stopped before userspace after randomdev_wait_until_seeded messages; terminated and original image digest unchanged. Cause not established.
usb_control.second_boot: Same image with virtio-rng-pci added: reached userspace and a local root console.
usb_control.root: cd9660 read-only ISO9660 label over da0
usb_control.inference: The shared raw-disk root access prevents the sibling writable mount; an independently attached filesystem from the same image writes successfully. No global GEOM protection override was applied.

independent_write_control.method: Attach the tested image to the separate retained-root FreeBSD worker; verify allocated virtual disk serial before selecting its trace partition
independent_write_control.controller_contents: independent native FreeBSD FAT32 write and remount control

limitations: Both images retain the old live root and are not the complete current-Omarchy RAM installer.
The end-to-end builder artifact and the booted append-control artifact have distinct identities; only the latter received USB boot and independent write tests.
Independent filesystem persistence does not establish default same-medium boot/install capture.
Default userspace persistence needs a qualified root arrangement that releases the installation disk, or another proven layout.
Raw logs and screenshots remain private; these development results are not lifecycle receipts.
